title: When stuff hits the fan, you’ve got two choices: anchor in, or scramble for safety
captions: Volatility doesn't test you. It reveals what you actually trust. Do you trust your system? Do you trust your edge or yourself? Or are you just chasing control just to outrun discomfort? Because when the market shakes or life does, you'll either anchor in or grasp for safety. Resilience isn't about pushing harder. It's about staying present under pressure. That's where clarity cuts through. That's when your power returns. And the same is true in trading and in life. Same nervous system. Drop resilience in the comments and I'll send you my free ebook, The Five Practices to Become a Better Trader.

title: Enhance Your Awareness for Trading Success #stockmarket
captions: let's talk about awareness what is awareness and how can you enhance it well awareness is simply being present and conscious to the trading decisions you make every day you want to help spot the biases you might have and that helps you stay focused you want to practice mindfulness to heighten your awareness and you want to take regular breaks to reset and to assess are you in a sense of clarity or are you being swayed by things beyond your control

title: Let's Discuss Discipline for Stocks #trading
captions: let's talk about discipline why is it important and how you can practice it as a Trader discipline is essential for you to have consistent trading success you have to set daily limits and you have to review them regularly you have to limit trades you have to focus on the quality over quantity and then you also must keep a trading journal and refine find your discipline over time unfortunately it's not one and done you have to reassess all the time and I would recommend you do this at least on a monthly basis

title: One Elite Trader's Kryptonite  - The Front Side of the Move #stockmarket #trading #coaching
captions: even the good Traders get themselves in trouble at particular times so I'm thinking of one Trader who I would just call a Hall of Fame Trader in our space gets himself in trouble by shorting stocks on the way up before they've shown weakness before the price action has confirmed that their thesis that hey the stock is overbought and should go down and they we we call it getting on the front side not to be too technical but getting the front side of a trade meaning shorting it before it's actually started to go down

captions: Andrew aiz shared about his climb to Mount epest and he talked about his own struggle with mindfulness and meditation and he said that right before he reached the summit between the conditions of the weather the freezing cold the fear he was having as he was climbing and even the ice that they were walking on he was forced to be in each step he took and he couldn't afford to think of anything else and he got that that was present moment awareness but imagine if each of you in your trading day were able to just pause and ask yourself am I actually looking at the market right now with no attachment to the past or the future and if not that's a reminder to bring yourself back

title: Stop 🛑 Trading with an Agenda
captions: Aloha everybody Welcome to My EQ Trader prep for the week of September 17th you may know that I've started to do live coaching on my YouTube channel the Wall Street coach on Wednesdays at 7 pm Eastern I hope you'll join us one of the topics that is repeatedly showing up is this concept of making up for a loss or uh trying to have a recovery over a big loss that perhaps took place in the past but I want to say might be a little controversial but you never make up for your losses and I really want you to step into this mindset because if you don't what happens is you step into every trading take you have with an agenda to make up for that loss and when you step in with an agenda you're not going to be able to see rationally or plainly what the market is doing you will have blinders so to speak on or a projection of what you want the market to do so you can make up your loss and that is never going to serve you I want you to actually think about each loss as a period at the end of it not a comma and so part of the reason I think that this temptation sits there is because it's hard for you to be with the loss it hurts to be with Colossus it makes you angry to be with your loss it makes you mad or frustrated that you didn't keep your word to yourself but you have to feel those feelings because part of feeling those feelings is actually going to keep you from doing it again so are they hard to be with feelings yes but if you're not with the truth that you did X Y or C you're more tempted to do it again so my suggestion this week is see if you can eradicate from your internal vocabulary or external vocabulary this concept of making up for a loss see if you can find way as hard as it might be to accept that law has put a period at the end of that sentence and then go back to your trading fresh with a clean slate let me know how it goes
